facts.raw_span: A 42-year-old man
underwent transthoracic echocardiography as part of a routine medical checkup
which revealed a left ventricular mass
He had no prior medical history
denied fever, weight loss, dyspnea, or other symptoms
his temperature was 36.5 °C
blood pressure 120/80 mm Hg
electrocardiogram showed normal sinus rhythm
A chest radiograph revealed no active lung lesions
Transthoracic echocardiography demonstrated a mobile, smooth, oval, pedunculated mass originating from the left ventricular lateral wall, measuring 1.34 × 1.9 cm
Contrast-enhanced chest computed tomography showed the mass attached to the interventricular septum with focal contrast enhancement

concepts.why: The patient has a mobile, smooth, oval, pedunculated mass originating from the left ventricular lateral wall, which is consistent with a left ventricular myxoma.
The patient has a left ventricular mass, which could be a fibroelastoma, a rare benign cardiac tumor.
The patient has a left ventricular mass, which could be a rhabdomyoma, a rare cardiac tumor.
The patient has a left ventricular mass, which could be a thrombus, although the echocardiography description suggests a more solid mass.
The patient has a left ventricular mass, which could be a sarcoma, a rare malignant cardiac tumor.
The patient has a left ventricular mass, which could be a lymphoma, a rare malignant cardiac tumor.
The patient has no clear evidence of infection, but infective endocarditis is a possible cause of a cardiac mass, although less likely given the absence of fever and other symptoms.
The patient has a left ventricular mass, which could be a metastasis from a primary malignancy elsewhere in the body, although there is no clear evidence of a primary tumor.
The mobile, smooth, oval, pedunculated mass with focal contrast enhancement is consistent with Papillary Fibroelastoma.

rationales.F03: Left ventricular mass is a key feature of myxoma and fibroelastoma.
rationales.F04: No prior medical history reduces the likelihood of conditions like infective endocarditis.
rationales.F05: Absence of symptoms like fever and weight loss reduces the likelihood of conditions like infective endocarditis and cardiac sarcoma.
rationales.F09: No active lung lesions on chest radiograph reduces the likelihood of conditions like pulmonary embolism or metastasis.
rationales.F10: Mobile, smooth, oval, pedunculated mass is characteristic of myxoma and fibroelastoma.
rationales.F11: Contrast enhancement on computed tomography is consistent with myxoma and fibroelastoma.
